papers.title: A systems biology network analysis of root resorption biomarkers and their clinical relevance in orthodontics: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: External apical root resorption is a frequently reported iatrogenic consequence of orthodontic tooth movement. This pilot study used an integrated systems biology approach to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers associated with orthodontic root resorption to support future functional research.
papers.summary: This pilot study applies systems biology network analysis to identify signaling pathways, key genes, and candidate salivary biomarkers linked to orthodontic root resorption. The findings aim to guide future functional research into this common iatrogenic side effect of orthodontic treatment.

papers.title: Endothelial SLC25A13 links glutamine metabolism to angiogenesis.
papers.abstract: Attention to exploring endothelial cell (EC) metabolism is increasing, but a holistic perspective on the metabolic adaptations of ECs during angiogenic proliferation is still missing. Here, we use a previously in-house developed computational EC-adapted genome-scale metabolic model that recapitulates known metabolic features in proliferating ECs to predict novel pathways central to biomass synthesis. We unveil the metabolic function of the glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13, previously overlooked in ECs, as a key regulator of glutamine utilization and provide evidence regarding its contri
papers.summary: This study uses an endothelial cell-adapted genome-scale metabolic model to predict metabolic pathways important for angiogenesis, identifying the mitochondrial glutamate-aspartate antiporter SLC25A13 as a previously overlooked regulator of glutamine utilization in proliferating endothelial cells. The findings link SLC25A13-mediated glutamine metabolism to angiogenic proliferation, suggesting a new metabolic target for modulating blood vessel formation.

papers.title: Enhancing 3-hydroxypropionic acid production in Komagataella phaffii via methanol and formate co-feeding.
papers.abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a promising cell factory that can use CO2 derived methanol, a sustainable carbon (C1) source, for chemical production. Introducing the ß-alanine biosynthetic pathway alongside a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase (FDH) in K. phaffii enables the production of the platform chemical 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP). Co-feeding of formate and methanol (MeOH) was systematically explored to enhance cellular reducing power and improve 3-HP biosynthesis. Implementing a pulsed formate strategy alongside MeOH resulted in up to a 20.7% increase in 3-HP per gram of MeOH (Yg3-HP gM
papers.summary: This study engineers Komagataella phaffii to produce 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP) from methanol by introducing a β-alanine pathway and a NADP+-dependent formate dehydrogenase. Co-feeding formate with methanol, especially in a pulsed strategy, boosts cellular reducing power and increases 3-HP yield per gram of methanol by up to 20.7%. The work demonstrates a metabolic engineering approach to improve C1-based chemical production.

papers.title: Harnessing computational intelligence for synthetic lethality: A roadmap from network biology to interpretable deep learning in precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Synthetic lethality (SL) is an emerging therapeutic paradigm in precision oncology that enables the selective targeting of cancer cells based on their specific genetic vulnerabilities. Despite its clinical promise, the enormous combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions poses a major challenge for experimental screening. This review provides a critical survey of computational SL discovery, moving beyond sequential descriptions to offer a comparative synthesis of architectures ranging from traditional network-based models to advanced graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. W
papers.summary: This review surveys computational methods for predicting synthetic lethal gene pairs in cancer, comparing traditional network-based approaches with modern graph transformers and knowledge graph reasoning. It argues that interpretable deep learning architectures can help navigate the vast combinatorial search space of gene-gene interactions more efficiently than experimental screening alone.

papers.title: Enterobacteriaceae for succinic acid biomanufacturing: metabolic blueprints, systems-level engineering and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Succinic acid (SA) is a key C4 platform molecule with wide industrial relevance, including bio-based polymers and solvents. Current reviews largely emphasize traditional producers (e.g., Actinobacillus, Mannheimia, and Basfia) and rarely synthesize progress in Enterobacteriaceae. Here, we close this gap by providing a systems-level review of SA biomanufacturing in Enterobacteriaceae, focusing on non-model genera (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) that combine fast growth, facultative anaerobiosis, broad feedstock utilization, and high engineering amenability. We outline the metabolic blue
papers.summary: This review synthesizes progress in engineering Enterobacteriaceae (Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Citrobacter) as microbial cell factories for succinic acid production, a key C4 platform chemical. It covers metabolic blueprints, systems-level engineering strategies, and future perspectives, filling a gap left by reviews focused on traditional producers like Actinobacillus and Mannheimia.

papers.title: Integrative Proteomics and Genome-Scale Modeling Elucidate Metabolic Flux Shifts in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CC-4414 Under Light Stress.
papers.abstract: The green microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii holds substantial promise as a photosynthetic cell factory for sustainable bioproduction, yet strain-specific metabolic responses to environmental stress remain underexplored. Here, we reconstructed a genome-scale metabolic network (GSMN) of the light-tolerant strain C. reinhardtii CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with integrative proteomics. The resulting model, designated iYH2021, comprises 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites, representing the first genome-scale metabolic reconstruction reported for this strain. To elucid
papers.summary: This study reconstructed the first genome-scale metabolic network for the light-tolerant Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with proteomics, producing a model called iYH2021 with 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites. The model was used to analyze metabolic flux shifts under light stress, revealing strain-specific metabolic responses relevant to using this alga as a photosynthetic cell factory.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the limitations of existing module discovery methods by providing direct biological interpretability and reducing redundancy compared to pathway-based approaches. The tool aims to translate complex molecular alterations into coherent functional insights.

papers.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
papers.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul
papers.summary: This study examined how expression of the protamine genes PRM1 and PRM2 relates to semen quality in rams, finding that their expression levels are associated with total sperm motility. Using gene regulatory network analysis, the authors also explored potential upstream regulators of these genes. The work extends protamine biology from model organisms and humans into an agriculturally relevant livestock species.

papers.title: KBase: Open-source Platform for Collaborative Biological Data Analysis and Publication.
papers.abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy's Systems Biology Knowledgebase (KBase; www.kbase.us) is an open, collaborative platform that integrates data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recently, KBase expanded as a comprehensive, multi-omics ecosystem. KBase enables representation of scientific samples, long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, and scalable modeling of microbial communities across diverse environments. KBase also generates digital notebooks as citable, executable research objects that link data
papers.summary: KBase is an open-source, collaborative platform that integrates multi-omics data, models, and analysis tools to accelerate discovery in microbiology, plant biology, and environmental systems. Recent expansions add long-read sequence analysis, protein structure integration, scalable microbial community modeling, and executable digital notebooks as citable research objects.

papers.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference depends on high-quality prior knowledge, yet curated priors are often incomplete or unavailable across species and cell types. We present GLM-Prior, a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence. We integrate GLM-Prior with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline that combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data for prior-conditioned GRN inference. Across six cell-line contexts, GLM-Prior performance scales with positive label abundance and TF coverage, showing above-chance a
papers.summary: GLM-Prior is a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions directly from nucleotide sequence, addressing the frequent lack of curated prior knowledge for gene regulatory network inference. Integrated with PMF-GRN in a dual-stage pipeline, it combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression data for prior-conditioned GRN inference, with performance scaling with positive label abundance and TF coverage across six cell-line contexts.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Host Regulatory and Immune Networks with Inferred Dysbiosis Relevance in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence suggests that intestinal microbial dysbiosis contributes to colorectal tumorigenesis by reshaping host molecular signaling and the tumor immune microenvironment. However, the molecular mechanisms linking microbiome-associated alterations to host regulatory networks and disease progression remain incompletely understood. Objective: This study aimed to identify the microbiome-associated molecular regulators and immune modulators involved in colorectal cancer through an
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to identify host regulatory and immune networks in colorectal cancer that are associated with inferred microbial dysbiosis. The authors link microbiome-related alterations to molecular regulators and immune modulators, aiming to clarify how dysbiosis may contribute to tumor progression.

papers.title: Selection favors cost-ordered adaptive mutational paths in a stress-magnitude-dependent manner.
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to stress requires adaptive strategies beyond canonical regulatory mechanisms. Stress varies, both qualitatively and quantitatively, across physiological niches and exerts distinct selection pressures on colonizing bacteria. Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies to withstand various stressful conditions, yet how they tailor their responses to different magnitudes of the same stressor remains poorly understood. We used multiple adaptive laboratory evolution experiments of Escherichia coli across varying paraquat concentrations and genetic backgrounds to dissect adaptive st
papers.summary: This study uses adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli under different concentrations of the oxidative stressor paraquat to show that selection favors mutational paths whose fitness costs are ordered, and that this ordering depends on stress magnitude. The findings suggest that the quantitative level of a stressor shapes which adaptive trajectories are accessible, with low-cost mutations preferred under some conditions and higher-cost paths becoming viable as stress intensifies.

papers.title: Integrated Cell-Based Transcriptomic and Pathway Profiling Enables Scalable Functional Screening of Bioactive Microalgal Extracts.
papers.abstract: Background: Microalgae and cyanobacteria represent a largely unexplored source of bioactive compounds, but systematic screening of extensive strain collections is limited by the cost and complexity of conventional chemical and pharmacological characterization. Here, we evaluated a scalable functional screening strategy integrating human cell-based gene expression profiling, quantitative molecular pathway analysis, and direct cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive microalgal and cyanobacterial extracts for subsequent investigation. Results: Forty-eight extracts were screened using HL-60 h
papers.summary: This study presents a scalable functional screening pipeline that combines human cell-based transcriptomic profiling, pathway analysis, and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize bioactive compounds from microalgae and cyanobacteria. Screening 48 extracts demonstrated that this integrated approach can efficiently identify promising extracts for further investigation, addressing the bottleneck of conventional chemical characterization.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data.
papers.abstract: While targeted therapies have reshaped the clinical management of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs), primary non-response remains a major obstacle for many patients. Combining two targeted therapies is an emerging strategy to overcome this therapeutic ceiling, but the number of possible drug pairs makes prioritization difficult. For this objective, we present mitigation of non-response signature (MNRS), a computational approach that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six IMIDs treated with different targeted therapies to identify the most promising drug combinations.
papers.summary: The authors present MNRS, a systems biology computational method that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomic data from six immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize promising combinations of targeted therapies. By identifying drug pairs that counteract non-response signatures, the approach aims to help overcome primary non-response to single targeted therapies.

papers.title: A Human Accelerated Region Drives Opposing Heterochronic Changes in Craniofacial and Limb Development.
papers.abstract: Many human developmental processes proceed over a prolonged timescale compared to other primates, a phenomenon known as heterochrony. Human accelerated regions (HARs), which encode transcriptional enhancers with human-specific activity, have been implicated in the evolution of novel human traits. However, their contributions to changes in developmental timing remain unknown. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing and developmental trajectory analyses in a genetically humanized mouse model of the HAR HACNS1 , we show that HACNS1 drives heterochronic shifts in opposite directions during craniofacia
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses a humanized mouse model and single-nucleus RNA sequencing to show that the human accelerated region HACNS1, a transcriptional enhancer, drives opposite changes in developmental timing (heterochrony) in craniofacial versus limb development. The findings link a human-specific enhancer to the evolution of altered developmental schedules underlying distinct human anatomical traits.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Gene-Network Analysis Prioritise a TREM2/LGALS3/GPNMB Scar-Associated Macrophage Programme in Human Liver Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: Macrophages organise the fibrotic niche of liver cirrhosis. The scar-associated macrophage state is well described, but the genes that define it have rarely been ranked in an unbiased, model-based way, and the statistical limits of such re-analyses are seldom reported. Here we set out to re-derive the scar-associated macrophage programme without supervision, to rank its constituent genes by convergent computational evidence, and to state explicitly what a cohort of this size can and cannot support. We re-analysed 58,358 single-cell transcriptomes from five uninjured and five cirrhotic human li
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed 58,358 single-cell transcriptomes from human uninjured and cirrhotic livers using explainable AI and gene-network analysis to unbiasedly rank genes defining scar-associated macrophages. They converge on a TREM2/LGALS3/GPNMB programme as central to this fibrotic macrophage state, while explicitly reporting the statistical limits of their cohort size.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) govern many cell processes. While multistability and oscillations are common GRN dynamics, they are typically studied and engineered in isolation. Here, we challenge this separation using the AC-DC circuit, a minimal three-gene network that merges the classical toggle switch and repressilator. Using a thermodynamic formalism and Bayesian inference, we show that a single-inducer version of the circuit displays diverse multifunctional dynamics, including coexistence of oscillations and multistability. We explore robustness, classify emergent behaviors, and analyze
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the AC-DC genetic circuit, a minimal three-gene network combining a toggle switch and a repressilator, to show that a single circuit can simultaneously exhibit multiple dynamical behaviors like oscillations and multistability. Using thermodynamic modeling and Bayesian inference, the authors map a 'zoo' of emergent dynamics, classify them, and assess robustness. The work challenges the traditional separation of these behaviors and suggests that multifunctionality is a common feature of gene regulatory networks.

papers.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa
papers.summary: The authors present scstruc, an R package for learning Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomic data and for evaluating the structural accuracy of the inferred networks in capturing causal gene-gene relationships. This addresses a gap in widely available software for both BN learning and causal assessment from single-cell data.

papers.title: Bayesian inference of gene regulatory networks at stochastic steady state.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) form the regulatory backbone that coordinates gene expression. The architecture of GRNs shapes their function and constrains the biochemical pathways through which information flows. Inferring the structure of regulatory interactions is thus essential for understanding biological systems and designing targeted therapies. Despite substantial progress in GRN inference, most approaches-from statistical methods to deep learning-do not take into account fundamental biochemical processes that drive regulatory dynamics. To address this shortcoming, here, we present a n
papers.journal: Journal of the Royal Society, Interface
papers.summary: The authors present a Bayesian method for inferring gene regulatory network structure that explicitly models the underlying biochemical dynamics of gene expression at stochastic steady state. By incorporating mechanistic biochemical processes rather than treating network inference as a purely statistical pattern-matching problem, the approach aims to produce more biologically grounded and interpretable network reconstructions.

papers.title: Integrating Metabolic Modeling and Targeted Supplementation for the Rapid Detection of Clostridium tyrobutyricum in Dairy Products.
papers.abstract: Clostridium tyrobutyricum is a major cause of late blowing defects (LBDs) in cheese, resulting in substantial economic losses. Early detection is critical for maintaining product quality. In this study, we developed a rapid detection approach integrating genome-scale metabolic modeling (GEM) with systematic culture optimization. Three media were evaluated, identifying RCM at 38.5 °C as the optimal condition for reducing the lag phase. Flux Balance Analysis (FBA) revealed that targeted supplementation with magnesium, zinc, Vitamin B6, and L-tryptophan significantly enhanced metabolic flux throu
papers.summary: This study combines genome-scale metabolic modeling with culture optimization to rapidly detect Clostridium tyrobutyricum, a bacterium causing late blowing defects in cheese. The authors identified optimal growth conditions (RCM medium at 38.5 °C) and used flux balance analysis to show that supplementing with magnesium, zinc, vitamin B6, and L-tryptophan boosts metabolic flux, enabling faster detection.

papers.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution enables carbon-negative mixotrophic fermentation and enhanced chain elongation in Clostridium sp. JS66.
papers.abstract: Improving carbon recovery during sugar fermentation remains a major challenge because a substantial fraction of substrate carbon is lost as CO2 during central metabolism. To overcome this limitation, Clostridium sp. JS66 (JS66), an acetogen producing hexanoic acid from glucose, was subjected to adaptive laboratory evolution under autotrophic CO2/H2 conditions to enhance H2-assisted CO2 reassimilation during glucose fermentation. The evolved strain, ALECO2, exhibited CO2 consumption without a lag phase under autotrophic conditions and reached a 9.5-fold higher CO2 uptake rate than JS66. Under f
papers.summary: Researchers used adaptive laboratory evolution to improve Clostridium sp. JS66, an acetogen that produces hexanoic acid from glucose, by selecting for enhanced CO2/H2 reassimilation. The evolved strain, ALECO2, consumed CO2 without a lag phase and achieved a 9.5-fold higher CO2 uptake rate than the parent strain, enabling carbon-negative mixotrophic fermentation and improved chain elongation.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling with reverse mapping links host perturbations to Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Understanding host-pathogen interactions during Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection has largely relied on identifying bacterial genes essential for intracellular survival. However, conventional reverse genetics approaches often overlook host pathways that regulate Mtb growth. Here, we developed a backtracing strategy to link host metabolic modulators with specific Mtb proteins. A genome-scale host metabolic model integrated with lung transcriptomic data from H37Rv-infected mice predicted 18 host proteins essential for Mtb survival. We validated this through pharmacological inhibition, s
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational backtracing strategy that integrates a genome-scale host metabolic model with lung transcriptomic data from Mtb-infected mice to identify host proteins essential for bacterial survival. They predicted 18 such host proteins and validated them through pharmacological inhibition, linking host metabolic perturbations to specific Mtb proteins. This approach offers a new way to uncover host-directed targets for tuberculosis therapy beyond conventional bacterial-focused reverse genetics.

papers.title: CardamomOT: A mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. In earlier work, we introduced CARDAMOM, an algorithm that uses temporal snapshots of scRNA-seq data to calibrate a GRN-driven mechanistic model of gene expression. However, this method had several limitations: it could only rely on the relative ordering o
papers.summary: The authors present CardamomOT, a mechanistic optimal transport framework that infers gene regulatory networks, reconstructs cellular trajectories, and enables generative modeling from single-cell RNA-seq data. It extends their earlier CARDAMOM method by using optimal transport to overcome limitations of relying only on relative temporal ordering, allowing more robust calibration of GRN-driven models of gene expression.

papers.title: Whole-cell spatiotemporal model and multimodal data illuminate the multiscale light responses in a photosynthetic bacterium.
papers.abstract: Photosynthetic microorganisms rely on multiple central carbon metabolism pathways to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles. Mechanistic insight into the regulatory dynamics of this adaptation requires integrating processes that operate across disparate timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications (PTMs) to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. Here, we develop a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that explicitly represents the spatial, subcellular organi
papers.summary: This paper presents a whole-cell 4D (3D + time) computational model of the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus marinus MED4 that integrates spatial subcellular organization with regulatory dynamics across multiple timescales, from rapid redox-dependent post-translational modifications to slower changes in protein expression and metabolic pathway usage. By combining the model with multimodal data, the authors illuminate how this photosynthetic bacterium coordinates its central carbon metabolism to adapt to fluctuating light and energy availability across diel cycles.

papers.title: Rhizobia bacteroid transcription helps to coordinate the soybean nodule drought response.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max L. [Merr.]) nitrogen fixation is sensitive to soil drying and is an important target for improving soybean drought resilience. Transcriptional regulation of the nodule drought response and the influence of symbiotic rhizobia are not well understood. We measured whole-plant responses to mild and moderate soil moisture deficit (41% and 20% of field capacity) alongside the nodule transcriptome, including soybean and Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens transcripts, in two soybean genotypes ('Benning' and PI 471938) that were previously found to have diverging nitrogen fixation droug
papers.summary: This study examined how soybean nodules respond to mild and moderate drought at the whole-plant and transcriptome level, including both soybean and its symbiotic rhizobia (Bradyrhizobium diazoefficiens) gene expression. The authors found that rhizobia bacteroid transcription actively contributes to coordinating the nodule drought response, and that two soybean genotypes with differing nitrogen fixation drought tolerance show distinct transcriptional patterns. This highlights the symbiotic bacterial partner as a key, often overlooked player in plant drought resilience.

papers.title: Thermo-flux: generation and analysis of thermodynamic-stoichiometric metabolic network models.
papers.abstract: Metabolic modeling with stoichiometric models and flux balance analysis (FBA) has greatly advanced our understanding of metabolism. However, valid FBA predictions require mechanistically correct constraints. Thermodynamic constraints can increase the mechanistic foundations of stoichiometric models and reduce the solution space, but incorporating them has so far required cumbersome manual effort. To circumvent manual curation, we introduce 'Thermo-Flux', a semi-automated Python package that converts stoichiometric models into comprehensive thermodynamic-stoichiometric models. 'Thermo-Flux' ena
papers.summary: Thermo-Flux is a semi-automated Python package that converts standard stoichiometric metabolic models into thermodynamic-stoichiometric models, adding thermodynamic constraints without the usual manual curation effort. This improves the mechanistic accuracy of flux balance analysis predictions and reduces the feasible solution space, making metabolic modeling more reliable.

papers.title: From plasmid sequence to process design: A computational analysis of metabolism in the context of plasmid DNA manufacturing.
papers.abstract: Detailed understanding of plasmid-host physiological interactions and recombinant protein expression is crucial for the design and optimization of plasmid DNA (pDNA) manufacturing processes. Successfully transformed host cells carrying one or more copies of a particular plasmid exhibit modified metabolic behavior which may include reduced specific growth rate, increased metabolic resource cycling (ATP/ADP, NAD/NADH, NADP/NADPH) and, in some cases, even modified nutrient uptake and metabolite secretion rates. Mapping plasmid design features to critical process parameters (CPPs), such as specifi
papers.summary: This paper uses computational metabolic modeling to analyze how plasmid DNA (pDNA) production alters host cell physiology, including growth rate, energy cofactor cycling, and nutrient uptake/secretion. The goal is to connect specific plasmid design features to critical process parameters, aiding rational design and optimization of pDNA manufacturing. It provides a systems-level framework linking plasmid sequence characteristics to bioprocess outcomes.

papers.title: Systems biology-driven drug repurposing in glioblastoma via antigen and pathway mapping.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with limited treatment options and poor patient survival. This study aimed to identify key genes and altered pathways in GBM and to explore potential drug-repurposing candidates using a systems biology approach.
papers.summary: This study applies a systems biology approach to glioblastoma, integrating gene expression and pathway data to identify key altered genes and pathways. The authors then use these molecular signatures to map and prioritize existing drugs as potential repurposing candidates for GBM treatment.

papers.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: Evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species.
papers.abstract: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension. We show that in simple organisms, aging is governed by a limited number of high-leverage pathways, whereas in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems c
papers.summary: This review proposes a unifying framework explaining why lifespan-extending interventions that work well in simple organisms (like yeast and worms) lose efficacy in mammals. The authors argue that aging in simple organisms is controlled by a few high-leverage pathways, while in mammals it emerges from distributed, multi-tissue regulatory systems that resist single-target interventions, shifting the challenge from pathway manipulation to system-level buffering.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (e.g., GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, ARACNe). Rather than selecting a single method or averaging all methods, the classifier learns edge-specific weights, and the authors also provide a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that uses supervised contrastive learning to pretrain gene representations on a shared human-mouse gene space, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses common challenges in GRN inference such as noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts by modeling gene-cell expression as a multi-relational heterograph. The method is benchmarked on BEELINE datasets, aiming to improve single-cell GRN prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Single-cell virtual knockout network perturbation prioritizes candidate regulators of beta-cell functional failure in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction is a central feature of type 2 diabetes (T2D), but disease-associated transcriptional changes alone cannot distinguish likely regulatory drivers from secondary stress markers. Single-cell transcriptomics resolves beta-cell heterogeneity across disease states, while virtual-knockout network analysis estimates transcriptional effects after perturbing selected genes. We combined human islet single-cell RNA sequencing, beta-cell functional-state modeling, candidate scoring, scTenifoldKnk virtual knockout, and external validation to prioritize regulators
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing of human pancreatic islets with virtual-knockout network perturbation (scTenifoldKnk) to distinguish regulatory drivers of beta-cell failure in type 2 diabetes from secondary stress markers. By modeling beta-cell functional states and scoring candidate regulators, the authors prioritize genes whose network perturbation most affects beta-cell function, with external validation. The approach offers a way to move beyond correlative disease-associated expression changes toward causal regulatory candidates.

papers.title: Host-directed therapeutics against antimicrobial-resistant bacterial infections: emerging roles of multi-omics and systems biology.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence and global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), coupled with the limited development of new antimicrobial agents, have intensified concerns regarding a major global public health crisis. Although antibiotic resistance is primarily driven by microbial mechanisms, host immune and inflammatory responses also play critical roles in determining infection outcomes, pathogen persistence, and treatment efficacy. In this context, host-directed therapies (HDTs) have emerged as a promising complementary strategy by modulating host pathways to enhance antimicrobial immunity
papers.summary: This review discusses how host-directed therapies (HDTs) can complement traditional antibiotics by modulating the host's immune and inflammatory responses to combat antimicrobial-resistant infections. It highlights the emerging role of multi-omics and systems biology approaches in identifying host pathways and biomarkers that could be targeted for therapy. The paper argues that integrating these technologies can accelerate the development of new treatment strategies against AMR.

papers.title: Neuro-psycho MMSig: multimodal mechanism enrichment platform for neuropsychiatric disorders.
papers.abstract: Understanding the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders requires integrating multimodal data.
papers.summary: The paper introduces Neuro-psycho MMSig, a platform designed to integrate multimodal data for enriching mechanistic understanding of neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. It aims to help researchers connect diverse data types to uncover biological mechanisms underlying these complex conditions.

papers.title: Evolution, disciplinary integration, and frontiers of multi-omics and single-cell technologies in periodontology: a bibliometric analysis (2000-2025) with an early-2026 frontier update.
papers.abstract: The field of periodontology is undergoing a paradigm shift from traditional microbiology to systems biology, driven by advancements in multi-omics and single-cell technologies. Despite the rapid surge in publications, a Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC)-based bibliometric and scientometric analysis mapping the evolutionary trajectory and emerging frontiers of these technologies in periodontal research remains needed. We performed a bibliometric and scientometric analysis of literature published from 2000 to 2025, with records from early 2026 used only as an exploratory frontier update, us
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps 25 years of multi-omics and single-cell technology research in periodontology, showing a paradigm shift from traditional microbiology toward systems biology approaches. The study identifies evolutionary trends, disciplinary integration patterns, and emerging research frontiers, with an exploratory update from early 2026 records.

papers.title: Probiogenomics as a Computational Biotechnology Framework: Safety-Gated Genome Analytics for Candidate Probiotic Prioritization and Validation.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing has transformed probiotic discovery into a strain-resolved computational problem, but genome data alone cannot establish probiotic efficacy, complete safety, or regulatory acceptability. This review frames probiogenomics as a safety-gated decision-support framework for candidate probiotic prioritization and validation. papers.summary: This review proposes probiogenomics as a computational framework that uses whole-genome sequencing data to prioritize and validate candidate probiotics, with safety screening as a mandatory gate. It integrates strain provenance, genome quality, taxonomic confidence, antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, mobile elements, and metabolite screening into a decision-support pipeline. The authors emphasize that genomic data alone cannot prove probiotic efficacy or regulatory acceptability, so the framework is positioned as a prioritization tool rather than a definitive validation method.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study integrates computational toxicology with multi-omics data to investigate whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The authors use systems biology approaches to link PFOA exposure to molecular pathways implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction.
